titles: Creator name first, then the bet or question in plain verbs, max 6 words. Never put the result in the title: 'Red Card', 'Copper' and 'Hang On' all gave away the payoff.
Phrase the stake as a question ('Can Kai Get Ray Through?'). Skip trivia ('Japan's Most Popular Dog') and vague teases ('Can't Believe What Happens').
Use one or two emoji at the end only. Drop the flag stacks.
hooks: Max 6 words, and add the stake the narrator didn't. If the hook and narrator say the same thing, cut one.
Ask whether it happens; never announce the outcome ('ONE HIT AWAY', 'HIS NAME IS REALLY UP THERE'). State what's on the line ('LOSE AND THE STREAM ENDS').
Cut vague teases like 'WAIT FOR HIS LIFE ADVICE'.
clip_picks: Only cut moments with a one-line spoken premise (bet, guess, countdown, question, argument). Speed or Kai with athletes and celebrities come first, then Kai with Ray.
Skip visual-only moments (crowds, dogs, clinches, boss-fight buildups, walk-ins). If it isn't funny read aloud, skip it.
Don't post two clips of the same moment (the two dubstep clips). Pick the one with the named guest.
Mine Jynxzi rank guessing as a series, but state the premise in the first line.
length_and_pacing: Stop cutting every clip to 53s. Start ≤2s before the stake line, end ≤2s after the payoff, and aim for 15-30s. Most breakouts run 11-26s.
End on the payoff line and cut trailing banter so the clip loops.
posting: Post 1-2 clips a day within hours of the stream. Clips 5-7 days old compete with hundreds of other clippers and sit at 0 views.
Check Studio for limits, duplicate-content flags and Shorts-feed serving, since every clip sits at 0-16 views with n/a analytics. After 48h, judge on 3s retention and Shorts-feed share.
Confirm scheduled clips went public. The earlier review flagged four as private.

money.idea: Apply to paid clipping campaigns beyond N3on, focusing on Speed, Kai and Adin-style creators
money.why: The channel already clips these streamers. Campaigns pay on views, and views aren't blocked by YPP's 0/1000 subs and 40/10M views.
money.first_step: Read the N3on campaign rules (allowed sources, length, payout basis) and submit 3 rewritten 15-30s clips to it this week. Then look for other campaigns covering Speed or Kai.

money.idea: Build a Jynxzi rank-guessing Shorts series as an owned format
money.why: The premise (guessing ranks) is repeatable and gives a one-line spoken hook, which the audit favors. A series can earn subs in a way scattered clips don't.
money.first_step: Cut 3 rank-guess clips from the 'ABSURD GUESSING RANKS' stream with the premise stated in the first 2 seconds and 'Part N' in the title.

money.idea: Long-form compilation videos of the best Speed/Kai premise moments
money.why: The Shorts are far from YPP thresholds. Longer videos can be monetized separately once the channel qualifies, and compilations reuse the same cuts.
money.first_step: After 2 weeks, take the top 8 clips by 3s retention and ask whether any streamer's clip policy allows compilations before editing one.

money.idea: Affiliate links or merch only after reaching a subscriber base
money.why: At 0 subs and about 40 views, there's no audience to convert. A pinned link to something generic would earn nothing yet.
money.first_step: Do nothing now. Revisit when a Short passes 10k views and ask what its viewers want.

next_actions: Open Studio and check channel limits, duplicate-content flags and whether the clips are served in the Shorts feed. 0 views on 14 clips is a distribution problem before it is a content problem.
Confirm the scheduled clips are public, and check that none are still private.
Re-cut the Speed vs Cole Palmer bet and the Speed 'taller' argument to 15-30s with question titles. Post them as new clips, not edits, after fixing the stake-first openings.
Stop clipping visual-only moments (crowds, dogs, boss fights, clinches). Only cut clips with a one-line spoken premise, within hours of the stream.
After 48h, pull 3s retention and Shorts-feed share for the 10h to 21h clips and cut more of whichever pattern holds.
